cards.summary: Equity risk is measured as the variance of actual returns around an expected return, and the cost of equity adds a risk premium for the portion of that risk investors cannot diversify away. The capital asset pricing model is the most widely used framework.
cards.title: Equity Risk and Expected Return

cards.summary: Intrinsic valuation derives the value of an equity from the expected cash flows it generates, discounted at a rate that reflects their riskiness. Damodaran frames discounted cash flow valuation as the foundational approach for estimating the value of any asset.
cards.title: Intrinsic Valuation and Discounted Cash Flows

cards.summary: Measuring an equity's earnings requires separating recurring operating income from extraordinary items, discontinued operations, and accounting changes. Damodaran stresses that clean earnings inputs are essential to reliable equity valuation.
cards.title: Measuring Earnings from Financial Statements

cards.summary: Relative valuation prices an equity by applying a market multiple, such as the price-earnings ratio, drawn from comparable firms. Damodaran treats pricing multiples as a fast alternative to intrinsic discounted cash flow valuation.
cards.title: Relative Valuation Using Pricing Multiples
